name: agent-builder-agents-md-hygiene
body:
The distributed `agent-builder` agent template (`opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md`, product source embedded via `include_str!` and installed by `apg init` into `~/.opencode/agents/`) OWNS the hygiene of each repo's `AGENTS.md` — the repo-level agent guide — as part of its agent-management responsibility. Its main-write surface therefore also includes the repo-root `AGENTS.md`, committed on main alongside its `.opencode/agents/**` and `opencode.json` writes: an additional write path under the SAME carve-out 1 of `global.constraint.worktree-isolation`, which now counts FOUR main-write paths across the two carve-outs.

Required behaviour:
- GRANT: the agent-builder's main-checkout write surface includes the repo-root `AGENTS.md`, so the hygiene instruction is actually executable (a grant the prose cannot carry out would be a broken scaffold).
- NON-CONTRADICTION: it ensures `AGENTS.md` does NOT contradict the distributed-agent rules (the distributed suite, the generated roster, the push/tag policy, the two main-write carve-outs).
- NON-DUPLICATION: it ensures `AGENTS.md` does NOT DUPLICATE the canonical change-set process, which is owned SOLELY by the distributed `codebase-navigator` agent prompt (`requirements.requirement.navigator-staged-flow`). Where `AGENTS.md` restates the process, the agent-builder removes or REPOINTS that prose — referencing the navigator as the process owner — instead of restating it.
- NON-DESTRUCTIVE: it preserves ALL repo-specific content — build gates, test tiers, pipeline description, release steps, and every other repo-specific section — and never deletes guide content that is not a process duplicate or a contradiction.
- ONLY WHEN PRESENT: `AGENTS.md` is OPTIONAL per project; the agent-builder acts only when one exists and never manufactures an `AGENTS.md` merely to point at the process.
- UNIVERSAL: the rule applies to EVERY apg project, not only the apg repo. In the apg repo the repo-local `build-implementer` also touches `AGENTS.md`; that is a LOCAL, repo-specific arrangement, not a universal rule — a project may have neither a `build-implementer` nor an `AGENTS.md`, and the universal law makes `agent-builder` responsible for `AGENTS.md` hygiene regardless.

Acceptance criteria:
- `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` instructs the agent-builder to own `AGENTS.md` hygiene: it removes or repoints any duplication of the canonical process (referencing the navigator as the owner) and any contradiction of the distributed-agent rules.
- The template carries the non-destructive merge rule (every repo-specific section preserved), the only-when-present rule (no `AGENTS.md` is manufactured), and states the rule is universal across apg projects.
- The template's frontmatter write grants admit the repo-root `AGENTS.md` on the main checkout, alongside `.opencode/agents/**` and `opencode.json`.
- Scope is the one product-source file `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md`; the apg repo's own `AGENTS.md` and `.opencode/agents/**` are consumer artifacts refreshed out-of-band by the agent-builder after a release and are NOT edited by this change-set.
